chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

If a man falls ill between one Ramadan and the next, then recovers, then for every day he broke his fast, he owes the ransom of food, which is a mudd for each poor person. He said: And likewise in the expiation of the oath and the dhihar [verbal divorce], a mudd for a mudd. If he recovers in between the two Ramadans, then he only owes making up the fast. And if he was negligent with it and has recovered, then upon him is the charity and the fasting together for each day, a mudd, when he finishes that Ramadan.

key_terms.الظِّهَارُ: Dhihar (a form of verbal divorce in pre-Islamic and Islamic law)
key_terms.فِدْيَةُ طَعَامٍ: Ransom of food (compensation for missed fasts)
key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific unit of volume for food measurement

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who is ill during Ramadan and fails to make up the fasts before the next Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between temporary illness and persistent negligence in delaying Ramadan's fasts until the next Ramadan arrives. It establishes that while recovery before the new Ramadan requires only qada, prolonged delay due to carelessness incurs both fidya (one mud of food per day) and qada, a ruling also extended to kaffarat al-yamin and zihar. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing compensation for missed obligations with accountability for unjustified delays.
